page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance trade-off. Single-core CPU performance is weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also register in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression benchmarks. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached operations remains in the average tier, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density and average multi-core capabilities, the ecs.r5.4xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not demand high single-thread CPU speeds. It is suitable for database operations, Redis caching layers, and static web serving, where it achieves average throughput. It can also handle moderate multi-threaded tasks and small-scale language model inference, though performance drops to weak levels for medium-sized models.
